nodes.summary: description: Guide for creating effective skills. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Claude's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations.
Think of Claude as exploring a path: a narrow bridge with cliffs needs specific guardrails (low freedom), while an open field allows many routes (high freedom).
├── scripts/          - Executable code (Python/Bash/etc.)
Executable code (Python/Bash/etc.) for tasks that require deterministic reliability or are repeatedly rewritten.
- **Note**: Scripts may still need to be read by Claude for patching or environment-specific adjustments
A skill should only contain essential files that directly support its functionality. Do NOT create extraneous documentation or auxiliary files, including:

Keep SKILL.md body to the essentials and under 500 lines to minimize context bloat. Split content into separate files when approaching this limit. When splitting out content into other files, it is very important to reference them from SKILL.md and describe clearly when to read them, to ensure the reader of the skill knows they exist and when to us
4. Edit the skill (implement resources and write SKILL.md)

To create an effective skill, clearly understand concrete examples of how the skill will be used. This understanding can come from either direct user examples or generated examples that are validated with user feedback.

Docker sandbox workspaces are typically mounted via **virtiofs** (file sync between the host and Linux VM). Native Go and Rust binaries (esbuild, lightningcss, rollup, etc.) crash with mmap alignment failures when executed from virtiofs on aarch64. The fix is to install on the container's local ext4 filesystem and symlink back into the workspace.
```bash
bash scripts/install.sh
## Post-Install Verification
```bash
| Verification fails intermittently | Run the script again — native binary crashes can be non-deterministic on first load |

verify_one "esbuild" node -e "require('esbuild').transform('const x: number = 1',{loader:'ts'}).catch(()=>process.exit(1))" || FAIL=1

3. **读 `_meta.json.genre_detected`，按下表加载对应题材风格包**（analyze 识别的题材 → write 的 genre-styles 包），正文腔调/招式随之切换：
> **拆文产出格式**：analyze 落盘的完整文件树、`_meta.json` schema、Stage→文件映射，以及「story-short-write 怎么读这些产出」的下游消费规范，见 [references/output-contract.md](references/output-contract.md)。

nodes.summary: > Download Scribd documents, ebooks, and publications as PDF files directly from your browser. **This extension is currently in development and has not been released yet.**

Scribd Downloader is an upcoming browser extension designed to let users save documents and publications from Scribd's digital library without relying on third-party desktop applications or complicated workarounds. It will integrate directly into the browser so you can export content while browsing Scribd's catalog of ebooks, audiobooks, magazines,
- Download Scribd documents and publications as standard PDF files
- Save ebooks, magazine articles, and research papers for offline reading
- Export sheet music and user-uploaded documents from the Scribd library
**This extension is not yet available for download.** Development is in progress and a release date has not been announced. Sign up below to get notified when it launches.

Scribd renders documents and books using a custom viewer that converts pages into images and layered text, making it impossible to simply copy the content or save the page as a usable file. Even with an active subscription, Scribd limits offline access to its own mobile apps and does not offer a browser-based export or PDF download option for most
- Full-document PDF export from Scribd's web-based document viewer
- Page-range selection so you can download specific sections instead of entire files
- Sheet music export with original notation and formatting preserved
- Download queue for managing multiple documents without waiting between each one
2. Open Scribd in your browser and sign in to your account.

Never a whole section, never curated prose."

Write everything this skill produces, files and messages alike, in plain simple language. Keep technical terms that carry real meaning; explain each in plain words. Never use a dash or a hyphen as punctuati

| Edit existing root/nested AGENTS.md | ✅ maintains | /sync |

| Add a one line pointer to `design.md` (the UI design system) in the nearest AGENTS.md when a change establishes one | ✅ maintains (pointer only) | /sync |
| Create nested `<area>/AGENTS.md` for an area **net new in this change** | ✅ creates (diff = full area context) + adds root pointer | /sync |
| Create nested doc for an **already existing** undocumented area (only sliced by the diff) | ❌ flags "run /audit" | /audit |
| Create or restructure the **root** AGENTS.md | ❌ flags "run /audit" | /audit |

# Udemy Video Downloader — Save Course Lectures Offline, Any Quality

Video Downloader for Udemy is a browser extension that saves Udemy course videos to your computer. Navigate to any lecture in a course you are enrolled in, click the download button on the player, and the video saves as MP4. Bulk download entire courses with per-lecture selection. Quality up to 4K. 3 free downloads included.

Udemy does not provide a built-in download option for desktop browsers. The mobile app has an offline mode, but it is restrictive and time-limited. You cannot right-click and save lecture videos because they use streaming delivery, and generic download tools fail because they cannot authenticate with Udemy. This extension connects directly to Udemy
- Bulk course download — view all lectures, select with checkboxes, and download them all at once
- In-page download button built right into the Udemy video player controls
- Download progress tracking with real-time status
- Download history with search, filter, sort, and export
- Configurable settings for quality preferences, file naming, and download folder
3. **Open a lecture** — Navigate to any lecture in a course you are enrolled in.
4. **Download** — Click the download button on the player, use the extension popup, or select multiple lectures for bulk download. Videos save as MP4.
- Udemy students who want to save course videos for offline study
